Bring the best of human thought and AI automation together at your work. # Understanding Likert-scale data and calculating composite score. I have conducted a questionnaire without much knowing about Likert. Now I realized that I have both Likert-scale data and Likert-type questions. I think I can look at their descriptive statistics through different methods: mean and standard deviation for Likert-scale data and median and frequency for Likert-type. I am not good at how to calculate a composite score for the Likert-scale data either. I have answers for level of preference (5 items) of different adaptation tools regarding three climate change impacts (heatwave, flood, drought) separately. There are two groups of options in all three: concrete vs green. The green options can also be divided into three categories based on the scale (building, street, city). So I want to understand if I can calculate a composite score to understand the general tendency on scales based on the answers. I am open to any kind of suggestion regarding analyzing the tendency over the inquired options by combining the answers. kjetil b halvorsen's user avatar.
